From e34f77b09080c86c929153e2a72da26b4f8947ff Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chen Ni <nichen@iscas.ac.cn>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 15:26:49 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] gpio: loongson-64bit: Fix incorrect NULL check after
 devm_kcalloc()

Fix incorrect NULL check in loongson_gpio_init_irqchip().
The function checks chip->parent instead of chip->irq.parents.

Fixes: 03c146cb6cd1 ("gpio: loongson-64bit: Add support for Loongson-2K0300 SoC")
Signed-off-by: Chen Ni <nichen@iscas.ac.cn>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260205072649.3271158-1-nichen@iscas.ac.cn
Signed-off-by: Bartosz Golaszewski <bartosz.golaszewski@oss.qualcomm.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpio/gpio-loongson-64bit.c b/drivers/gpio/gpio-loongson-64bit.c
index 77d07e31366f..0fdf15faa344 100644
--- a/drivers/gpio/gpio-loongson-64bit.c
+++ b/drivers/gpio/gpio-loongson-64bit.c
@@ -263,7 +263,7 @@ static int loongson_gpio_init_irqchip(struct platform_device *pdev,
 	chip->irq.num_parents = data->intr_num;
 	chip->irq.parents = devm_kcalloc(&pdev->dev, data->intr_num,
 					 sizeof(*chip->irq.parents), GFP_KERNEL);
-	if (!chip->parent)
+	if (!chip->irq.parents)
 		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	for (i = 0; i < data->intr_num; i++) {
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a bug in the file `drivers/gpio/gpio-loongson-64bit.c`. The issue is an incorrect NULL check after a memory allocation.

### Modifications per File

**File: `drivers/gpio/gpio-loongson-64bit.c`**  
- *Line 266 (original)*: Changed `if (!chip->parent)` to `if (!chip->irq.parents)`.

### Relationships between Modifications

This is a single-line fix that corrects a copy-paste error. The function `loongson_gpio_init_irqchip()` allocates memory for `chip->irq.parents` using `devm_kcalloc()`. Previously, the subsequent NULL check mistakenly inspected `chip->parent` (a different field of the chip structure) instead of `chip->irq.parents`. This meant that if the allocation failed, the error would not be properly detected, leading to potential use of a null pointer. The fix ensures the correct member is checked, providing proper error handling for the memory allocation.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>if (!chip->parent)</text>
Reason:
After allocating memory for `chip->irq.parents` with `devm_kcalloc`, the code incorrectly checks `chip->parent` (a different field, likely a device pointer) instead of checking the allocated pointer. If the allocation fails (`chip->irq.parents` is NULL), this check passes (since `chip->parent` is typically non-NULL), so the function returns success and later accesses `chip->irq.parents[i]`, causing a null pointer dereference.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (!chip->irq.parents)</text>
Reason:
This change correctly checks the pointer returned by `devm_kcalloc` for `chip->irq.parents`. If allocation fails, the function returns `-ENOMEM`, preventing the null pointer dereference that would occur when the code later tries to assign IRQ numbers to `chip->irq.parents[i]`.
